title: The lake of questions
hookLine: Yudhishthira answers a yaksha by a deadly lake: the truth of dharma is hidden in a cave, and Mimamsa says it's heard, not seen
tomorrow: a generous warrior reaches heaven and is served gold to eat. why?

cards: Late in their years of exile, the five Pandava brothers are desperately thirsty. One brother, Nakula, goes looking for water and finds a clear lake. A voice says: answer my questions first, then drink.
He drinks anyway, and falls dead. The next brother comes, and the next, and the next. Each ignores the voice, drinks, and falls.
Then the eldest, Yudhishthira, arrives, sees his four brothers lying by the water, and doesn't drink. He says: ask. The voice belongs to a yaksha, a powerful spirit, and the questions come fast.

teach.b: One question is the one Mimamsa cared about most. What is the path? Yudhishthira's answer is well-known.
Argument doesn't settle it. The scriptures differ. No single sage's word is final.

The truth of dharma is hidden in a cave. So the path is the one the great have walked. The yaksha is pleased, reveals himself as Dharma, Yudhishthira's own father in disguise, and brings the brothers back to life.
Hidden in a cave: Mimamsa makes a close cousin of this point in a philosopher's voice.
Jaimini's second sutra: dharma is a good known through codana, the Veda's injunction, its plain do this. Two sutras later he says why.
Perception only grasps what's present to the senses, and dharma isn't sitting there in the present to be seen; its good lies in what the act brings about.
Film every moment of a shraddha and you'll see sesame, water, rice balls. You won't see the dharma. So where do Hindus find it?
Mimamsa says: in the words that ask for it. The law books add more marks: the Veda first, then the remembered teachings, then the conduct of good people, then what sits rightly with your own self.

teach.h: THE PATH THE GREAT HAVE WALKED.
teach.b: The conduct of good people is Yudhishthira's path, the one the great have walked.
It's why, when a child asks why we do this, an honest Hindu answer is often: because it was asked of us, and because the people we trust most did it before us.

how: Mimamsa teachers read the Veda's ritual lines as injunctions and hold that dharma is known through them rather than through the senses; Hindu law books name further marks of dharma: remembered tradition, the conduct of good people, and what sits rightly with oneself.

o: a school where dharma is known by the Veda's injunction
a school that finds dharma by argument alone
a school where dharma is seen in how a rite looks

games.q: the lake and the sutras — tap the pairs.

s: Jaimini says you can see dharma with your own eyes
perception only grasps what's present; dharma is known through injunction.
Yudhishthira tells the yaksha the truth of dharma is hidden in a cave
argument doesn't settle it and scriptures differ, so the path is the one the great have walked.
the yaksha turns out to be a demon
he's Dharma himself, Yudhishthira's father, and he brings the brothers back to life.

games.q: a cousin asks why your family offers rice balls at a shraddha. you can't prove what it does. by today's teaching, what's an honest answer?
o: "we can prove it works, just watch"
"it's asked of us, and the people we trust did it before us"
"there's no reason, so we should stop"
games.why: Mimamsa says dharma is known through the Veda's injunction, not seen; Yudhishthira adds the path the great have walked.

practice: Bring to mind one thing your family does that you can't fully explain: a fast day, a thread tied on the wrist, a lamp at dusk, a way of greeting elders.
Picture the people you've seen do it, one after another, back as far as you can go. If you pray, ask to understand it, and do it anyway. If you don't, simply thank the hands that passed it to you.

wordCard.voice: Mimamsa. The school that says dharma is known through codana, the Veda's injunction, because the senses only see what's present.

orig.note: Sanskrit: urging or injunction; in Mimamsa, the mark by which dharma is known.

carryVoice: Your line: dharma is heard, not seen. Hidden in a cave, Yudhishthira said, so walk the path the great have walked. Go gently.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Aranyaka (Vana) Parva, the yaksha's questions (critical edition 3.296–3.298): the brothers at the lake; 'the truth of dharma is hidden in a cave; the path is the one the great have walked'; the yaksha revealed as Dharma
Mimamsa Sutras 1.1.2 (dharma is a good characterized by injunction)
Mimamsa Sutras 1.1.4 (perception is not a means to know dharma, since it grasps only what is present)
Manusmriti 2.12 (the Veda, smriti, the conduct of the good, and what is pleasing to oneself: the marks of dharma)
